title: QBR Sparkline Kit: Standard + Enterprise Variants
body:
Purpose:
This is a lean, repeatable QBR "Sparkline" kit focused on two lanes: a light Standard deck for expansion/engagement conversations and a deeper Enterprise deck for renewal + executive alignment. The goal is speed-to-quality: runbooks and slide microcopy you can drop into a deck quickly, plus a one-page renewal velocity tracker and a playbook checklist for next steps.

Audience:
- Customer Success Managers (ACMs, EAMs) running QBRs
- CS leadership prepping exec summaries
- Solutions Engineers joining Enterprise renewals

How to use this file (quick):
1) Pick lane: Standard or Enterprise.
2) Populate the headline KPIs from the renewal tracker (section below).
3) Use the slide microcopy below instead of building from scratch; adjust metrics and customer quotes.
4) Run the playbook checklist 48–24 hours before the meeting.

Timing guidance: Standard QBR = 30–45 min; Enterprise QBR = 60–90 min (with execs and SEs).

SECTION A — Standard QBR (one-pager + 6 slides)
Core objective: Surface value, show growth opportunity, agree on 1–2 next actions to increase usage or move toward renewal.
Slide 0 - Cover (1 line): "Quarterly Review: [Customer] — Health & Growth"
Slide 1 - 90-second summary (Sparkline headline): 2 bullets
  - Headline metric: ARR impact or feature-specific adoption (e.g., "+18% monthly inference calls")
  - Ask: Primary CTA (e.g., "Request enablement for Vector Search pilot")
Slide 2 - Health snapshot (single-row table): 4 cards — Usage trend sparkline, Cost per 1k tokens, Error rate, NPS indicator
Slide 3 - Top wins (3 short bullets with metrics and customer quote)
Slide 4 - Opportunities (2–3 expansion hooks; map to product plays such as Dedicated, Private, or Optimize recommendations)
Slide 5 - Roadmap alignment & blockers (1 short list: two product asks + operational blockers)
Slide 6 - Next steps & owner (action table: what, due date, owner)

SECTION B — Enterprise QBR (detailed, collaborative)
Core objective: Align execs on value realization, risk/motion toward renewal, and decision calendar. Bring SRE/SEs/Account Execs for technical and commercial decisions.
Suggested deck flow (12–18 slides):
Slide 0 - Cover: "Strategic Review & Renewal Readout — [Customer]"
Slide 1 - Executive TL;DR (3 lines): Renewal date, renewal signal (Green/Amber/Red), Ask (e.g., exec sponsor meeting)
Slide 2 - Contract snapshot: Term, current commit vs usage, overage exposure, next renewal window (table)
Slide 3 - Business outcomes (customer metrics tied to product: latency improvement, cost reduction, user conversion lift)
Slide 4 - Adoption & usage deep-dive: product areas, peak patterns, KV cache hit rate, batch sizes, queueing events
Slide 5 - Platform reliability: SLO adherence (p99 latency), incidents last 90d, mitigation actions taken
Slide 6 - Cost & efficiency: per-token unit economics, suggestions from Redwood Optimize (quantization recommendation + estimated $/month savings)
Slide 7 - Migration/Infra roadmap: private/dedicated options if requested, lift estimate, regression test plan
Slide 8 - Risk register: prioritized risks (tech, commercial, security), owner and mitigation status
Slide 9 - Case studies / peer benchmarks (concise datapoints from similar accounts)
Slide 10 - Commercial proposals: renewal scenarios (baseline, committed, enterprise reserved), financial impact table and dates
Slide 11 - Decision calendar & escalation path: what decisions are needed by when and who signs off
Slide 12 - Next steps & owner list (detailed RACI)
Optional appendix: audit logs, threat model summary for Private deployments, full incident timelines, model performance charts.

Slide microcopy examples (copy/paste ready):
- Exec TL;DR: "Renewal window: 2025-06-15 — Current usage at 86% of committed capacity. Recommended: move to 12-mo Reserved with 10% uplift to lock latency SLAs. Requested: Exec alignment call week of 2025-05-05."
- Risk bullet: "Cache fragmentation during peak caused 0.7s median p50 latency increase on 2024-11-04; mitigation: auto-prefix KV warmers deployed (owner: SRE)"

SECTION C — Renewal Velocity Tracker (one-page table you can paste into the deck)
Columns (one-row-per-renewal):
- Customer
- Renewal date
- Current ARR / Committed ARR
- Usage % vs commit
- Health signal (Green/Amber/Red)
- Net Revenue at Risk (est.)
- Primary blocker
- Next decision / due date
- Owner

Sample row (text only):
"Acme Digital | 2025-06-15 | $480k / $550k | 87% | Amber | $30k | Performance regression + compliance review | 2025-05-10 | Maya Patel"

Tracker tips: Keep this in a shared sheet linked in slide notes; refresh weekly and surface deltas (delta column optional). For Enterprise customers include a stakeholder map and procurement timeline column.

SECTION D — Playbook (pre-meeting, in-meeting, post-meeting)
Pre-meeting (48–72h):
- Sync with SE: validate latency/capacity figures; capture 1–2 screenshots of performance dashboards.
- Send pre-read: 1-page summary + ask. Attach renewal scenarios 2 days before.
- Confirm exec seat list & send calendar invite with agenda.

In-meeting (meeting script highlights):
- First 5 min: Exec TL;DR (state ask and renewal date)
- Next 15–30 min: Customer outcomes and evidence (data-driven)
- Next 10–20 min: Risks & mitigation + technical deep dive (SE)
- Final 10 min: Decisions & next steps; confirm owners and timelines

Post-meeting (24–72h):
- Send follow-up note with actions table and updated tracker row.
- Create Jira/Linear tasks for roadmapped items and tag SE and PM.
- Schedule decision checkpoint (15 min) 7–14 days before key due date.

Email templates (obvious placeholders in []):
Pre-read email:
"Subject: QBR + Renewal Pre-read — [Customer] — [Date]
Hi [Sponsor],
Attaching a short pre-read ahead of our QBR on [date]. TL;DR: we recommend [scenario], and would like an exec alignment call w/you and [stakeholders] the week of [week]. See attached summary and renewal scenarios.
Thanks,
[CSM name]"

Post-meeting follow up:
"Subject: Follow-up & Actions — QBR [Customer] [Date]
Thanks for taking time today. Per discussion, attaching the agreed actions and owners. Next checkpoint: [date]. Please let me know if anything is missing.
Best,
[CSM]"

SECTION E — Operational templates (checklist + dashboard links)
Mandatory pre-QBR dashboard exports:
- Token usage timeseries (90d)
- SLO adherence (p50/p95/p99)
- Cache hit rate and effective throughput
- Billing vs commit by day
\Suggested Dashboard links (placeholders to replace):
- Usage dashboard: https://console.redwood/example/usage/[tenant-id]
- Incidents timeline: https://console.redwood/example/incidents/[tenant-id]

One-page meeting checklist (copy into event notes):
- [ ] Pre-read shared 
- [ ] SE validated metrics 
- [ ] Exec attendees confirmed 
- [ ] Renewal scenarios attached 
- [ ] Slide deck exported as PDF (for procurement teams)

SECTION F — Notes & known open questions (use this as a scratch area)
- How aggressive should we price committed uplift for accounts in fast-growth verticals? (action: discuss with RevOps)
- For accounts with on-prem requirements, can we provide a two-phased Private rollout estimate within 10 business days? (owner: Solutions Eng)
- Consider adding a short slide showing Redwood Optimize savings simulation for common patterns (retrieval-heavy vs chat-heavy).

Appendix: quick glossary (short):
- Reserved = Dedicated capacity with monthly commit
- Private = VPC/on-prem deployment options
- KV = Key-value cache for autoregressive models

Change log (this doc):
- 2025-01-12 created (Maya Patel)
- 2025-02-20 updated: added Renewal Velocity Tracker row format and SE microcopy

End of doc.
